- [USER] User provided web search results related to algae and fertilizers.
- [USER] User's query: "What are the benefits of using algae as a bio stimulant instead of chemical fertilizer."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Algae can be used as a bio-stimulant in agriculture and has various benefits over chemical fertilizers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Algae can be a rich natural source of compounds with high biological activity against stress factors and fit well into recent strategies for the chemical industry, including the production of fertilizers and pesticides [[1](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-74703-3_10)].
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Chemical fertilizers improve crop quality and yield but have a negative impact on the environment and human health.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Organic fertilizers with algae are less likely to reach water bodies and other places where they should not be [[3](https://www.alganex.com/insights/algae-as-an-alternative-to-chemical-fertilizers-in-agriculture/)].
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Extensive research is ongoing to develop sustainable fertilizers that are non-toxic to the environment, and algal bio-fertilizers are among the best sustainable options [[4](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327143811_Algal_Biofertilizers_and_Plant_Growth_Stimulants_for_Sustainable_Agriculture)].
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Algal microflora has been found to promote biomass productivity and improve soil fertility, making algae environmentally favorable and pollution-free [[5](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1319562X22001759)].
- [USER] User provided additional web search results related to greenhouse gas emissions and chemical fertilizers.
- [USER] User's query: "Can you define the greenhouse gas emissions related to chemical NPK fertilizer per kilogram of fertilizer produced."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The production of chemical NPK fertilizers is associated with significant greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a potent greenhouse gas, with a global warming potential 300 times higher than carbon dioxide per pound.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium fertilizers components represent more than 200 million tonnes of production annually and share a large portion of the costs and emissions of GHGs, particularly carbon dioxide (CO2) [[3](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.energyfuels.2c00238)].
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Agricultural soils
